messages:
mara: Quick heads-up — ran a KV-cache-only quant experiment (FP8 on KV tensors, keep rest INT8) on the 13B service image. Wanted to share a short summary and get :eyes: on kernel pressure + cold-start tail.
vikram: nice, did you run both A100 and L4? any config differences?
mara: only ran A100L for the smoke due to limited L4 quota. Config: `--kv-quant=fp8 --global-quant=int8 --batcher=max_tokens=4096,timeout_ms=20` and pinned to model:v3-kvtest. Single-replica, 1 stream per GPU.
jen: can you paste the perf numbers? curious about 95p cold vs steady-state.
mara: baseline fp16 (no kv quant) steady p50 gen latency = 18ms/token, 95p = 42ms/token, peak GPU mem ~17.2GB. FP8-KV steady p50 = 19ms, 95p = 58ms, peak mem ~12.6GB. INT8-all steady p50 = 20ms, 95p = 60ms, peak mem ~11.4GB.
vikram: so FP8-KV gives ~4.6GB memory saving vs fp16 but increases cold 95p by ~16ms. did you see KV cache warmup behavior?
mara: yes — warm sessions (prefilled cache) have smaller deltas: FP8-KV warm 95p = 45ms. Cold sessions where KV needs to be materialized cause extra memcpy/kernel overhead. nvprof snapshot shows multiple small kernels for KV dequant + memcpy chaining.
simon: that suggests kernel-fanout pressure. did you test tile sizes / chunking tweaks?
mara: tried `kv-shard-size=64` -> reduced kernel launches by ~20% but made each kernel longer; 95p improved by 6-8ms but memory footprint unchanged. Also saw some fragmentation in the allocator trace.
jen: any OOMs or instability during the smoke deploy?
mara: one instance hit OOM when running 8 concurrent requests of long sequences (12k context) — that was with FP8-KV + other persistent caches. The pattern is: many small KV dequant kernels spike CUDA utilization leading to transient higher resident set.
perf-bot: perf snapshot: root=fp8-kv-smoke/1799102468, p50=19.3ms/tok, p95=57.8ms/tok, gpu_mem_peak=12.6GB, small-kernel-count=312.
mara: logs (trim): ```
[2026-10-12 14:03:11] INFO kv_dequant: launching 42 small kernels for shard 3
[2026-10-12 14:03:11] WARN cuda: transient alloc spike +1.1GB
[2026-10-12 14:03:12] INFO inference: completed request id=... latency=1213ms
```
vikram: interesting. I wonder if a dequant kernel fuse (dequant+prefetch) would reduce launches. Also consider pre-warming KV objects on first request to push latency to 1st request only.
simon: strategy idea: keep KV quantized on storage, but dequant on GPU asynchronously during generation so it overlaps with compute. That would shift overhead from tail to earlier in pipeline.
jen: rollout plan — what's safe for Dedicated customers? need to keep 95p within SLA (<=55ms for most tiers). FP8-KV borderline.
mara: my recommendation: don't enable FP8-KV by default. Offer as opt-in toggle with a canary on lower-tier models; add a canary that applies `kv-shard-size=64` and prefetch async dequant. Also add allocation guard to avoid OOM for long sequences.
vikram: agree. I'll prototype a fused kernel (dequant+copy) and run another smoke on L4 tomorrow.
mara: follow-ups: 1) simon + vikram to prototype kernel fusion, 2) eng-infra to add canary flag + throttling, 3) run broader sweep across 7/13/70B tomorrow and post results. I'll open a short doc with config snippets.
jen: thanks — please tag me on the doc and include perf-bot snapshots. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: started canary deploy for `model:v3-kvtest` -> env=canary-us-east -> id=canary-1799102468
mara: copying next steps into a quick checklist in case folks want to reuse the test harness: ```
# smoke steps
1. deploy model:v3-kvtest-canary
2. run workload: 50% long (12k), 50% short (512), concurrency=4
3. collect perf snapshots with perf-bot
4. check allocator logs for transient spikes
```
